title: Probability
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review
about: Teacher-verified mastery check. Written separately from the practice generators: different wordings, word problems, and an 'is this right?' item. Each item is worth 1 point. 'math' is the calculation in JavaScript form; the test checks the answer key's number (or fraction) against it.
directions: Show your work. Write probabilities as fractions in simplest form.

items.prompt: A bag has 4 red, 6 yellow and 2 green cubes. You pick one without looking. What is P(yellow)?
Using the same bag, what is P(not green)?
You roll a number cube. What is P(a number greater than 2)?
You flip a coin and spin a spinner with 5 equal sections numbered 1 to 5. What is the probability of tails and a 3?
A spinner has 4 equal sections, one of them blue. If you spin it 120 times, about how many times would you expect blue?
Sam says the probability of rolling a 6 on two number cubes is 1/6 + 1/6 = 1/3. Is he right? Find the probability.
A jar has 5 purple, 3 orange and 7 white marbles. You pick one without looking. What is P(orange)?
Using the same jar, what is P(purple or orange)?
You roll a number cube. What is P(an odd number)?
You roll a number cube and flip a coin. What is the probability of a number less than 3 and heads?
You roll a number cube 90 times. About how many times would you expect a 1 or a 2?
Kim says a bag with 2 red and 6 blue marbles gives P(red) = 2/6. Is she right? Find P(red).
